Shape the sound to your headphones and your taste, and keep loud songs from jumping out.

## New

- **Parametric equalizer** (Android 9 or newer). Add up to 10 filters, drag them on the graph, and hear the change right away. Each filter can be a peak, a low shelf or a high shelf, with its own frequency, gain and width. Find it in Settings > Audio Quality > Equalizer; it is off until you turn it on.
- **Presets.** Start from Bass, Vocal, Treble or Late night, or save your own tuning under a name. Long press one of your presets to delete it.
- **AutoEq import.** Download the `ParametricEQ.txt` file for your headphones from the AutoEq project, tap Import AutoEq and choose it.
- **Volume normalization.** Uses the volume info (ReplayGain) saved inside your songs to turn loud songs down, per song or per album. Find it in Settings > Audio Quality; it is off until you turn it on. Songs without that info play as they are.

## Improved

- **Softer highlights.** Rows in Settings, Help, dialogs and menus now light up with rounded corners and a little room around the text, instead of a sharp box, when you hover or press them.

## Good to know

- **A boost lowers the overall volume** by the same amount, so the sound never distorts. Turn your device volume up to make up for it.
- **ForYou Music rereads your songs once** after this update to pick up their volume info. Your favourites, playlists and play history are kept.
- **Volume info is read from MP3, FLAC, OGG and OPUS files.** M4A, AAC and WAV are not supported yet.
- **The equalizer is not available on Linux yet.**
- **Your files are never changed.** Both features only affect how songs sound while they play.
